evidence: docs/mcp-client-setup.md (added): "use `add-json` with the JSON in **single** quotes, so the shell passes the literal `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`"
examples/mcp-clients/claude/.mcp.json:14-17 (added): "keep the SINGLE quotes ... claude mcp add-json -s user rebar \\"

Named violating input: `claude mcp add-json -s user rebar "{\"type\":\"http\",\"headers\":{\"Authorization\":\"Bearer ${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}\"}}"`. `_operator_hits` returns [] for it, so test_no_operator_script_or_doc_puts_a_credential_in_argv and test_no_mcp_client_example_puts_a_credential_in_argv both pass.
The parametrized positive cases at lines 241-253 include no add-json shape.
dropped.finding: No `_OPERATOR_PATTERNS` entry catches the risky form of the newly recommended `claude mcp add-json` command. If the JSON argument is written in double quotes, the shell expands the PAT into argv. Every pattern (`curl-user`, `url-userinfo`, `http-password-arg`, `cli-value`, `awk-var`, `header-arg`) needs a `-u`/`--user`, userinfo, `--http-password`, `--value`, `-v` or `-H`/`--header` token, and none of them matches `add-json`. So the doc-line scan and the new example `$comment` scan both stay green on exactly the regression the new section warns about.
scenarios: A later edit to the guide or the Claude example swaps the single quotes for double quotes (e.g. to embed a different URL variable), and the guard does not fire.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add e.g. "add-json-arg": re.compile(r'''mcp\s+add-json\b.*?"[^"]*(?:authorization|bearer)[^"]*\$''', re.I | re.S) (and cover the line-continuation case), plus the double-quoted add-json line in the flag parametrize list and the documented single-quoted line in the pass list.
